accuracy.evidence: Curriculum placement checked against Development Matters (DfE, 2021): Expressive Arts and Design 3-4 'begin to develop complex stories using small-world equipment like animal sets, dolls and dolls houses', Communication and Language 3-4 'use longer sentences' and 'tell a long story', and the Reception ELG Speaking 'invent, adapt and recount narratives and stories with peers and their teacher'. The four-part story shape (opening, character, problem and resolution, ending) matches story-grammar research (Stein and Glenn 1979) and Applebee's (1978) account of young children moving from heaps of events to chains. No claim is made about written story structure, which belongs to later Writing Composition lessons.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the play-story slips named in the adult text: an ending phrase used as a start ('The end.' refused in the talk bubble, predict 1, challenge 'order'), play with no story words ('Tidy up time!' refused, challenge 'nostart'), a voice that does not fit the toy (wrong line on a toy names the cue, predict 2, p3, m2, challenge 'voice'), nothing happening ('They sit. They sit.' refused, predict 3, p5, challenge 'nothing') or ending too soon ('soon'), 'and then… and then…' never stopping ('noend', m1), walking off mid-story ('stop'), a fix the character could not do (Mouse and Teddy refused at the tree, m3, 'fix') and one right story (a repeated mix is refused, predict 4, m5, 'one').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagplaystory is a small-world story builder: story words dropped into a talk bubble, a toy dropped onto a play mat, character lines dragged onto the toy whose size and nature fit them, a problem card dropped into the middle followed by dragging the one toy able to solve it (Dragon flies up the tree), an ending slot, and a four-row who/where/oh-no/end mixer that tells a generated story and refuses a repeat. 990 Telling a story from picture cards (flagpicstory) orders a fixed picture sequence and 469 Playing with what I know (flagpretend) is about objects standing for others; neither invents a narrative. Lab shingle similarity is under 30% against every flag_*.js (lab_distinct gate passes).

lab_teaches.evidence: Each part of a story is found by trying it: 'The end.' in the talk bubble is refused with the reason, the mat and bubble accept only the right kind of piece, a mismatched line names the toy's cue ('Mouse is tiny and quiet'), 'They sit. They sit.' is refused until something happens, the tree refuses Mouse ('much too high for a tiny mouse') and Teddy ('that is why it is a problem'), the Start / Oh no! / The end strip ticks as each part is added, and the mixer reads back a whole new story each time. Done messages confirm only after the action.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'The end.' as a start (refused in the bubble), 'A big ROAR' for Mouse (the roar line is refused on Mouse and the squeak fits), 'Yes, that is a story' for Teddy just sitting (the sitting card is refused until an oh no happens) and 'Yes, just one' right story (the second, different mix is told as a new story).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions whose wrong options carry nine distinct slip messages: order (the end is how a story stops), nostart (tidy up time is not story words), voice (a tiny mouse squeaks, a big dragon roars), nothing (a story needs an oh no), soon (not the end yet), noend (and then… never stops), stop (walking off leaves the toys mid-story), fix (Mouse is too tiny to reach, choose a toy who can fly) and one (change a card, there are lots of stories).

readability.evidence: Kid text is four short paragraphs at FK grade about 0 (limit 5.0), using one- and two-syllable words (start, toy, talk, oh no, end); lab cards are one to eight words with emoji, read by a grown-up for a 3 to 4 year old. Adult text is FK 6.4 (limit 10.0) after splitting the story-shape and lab paragraphs into short sentences, and keeps the precise terms (small-world play, narrative, story grammar, opening, problem, resolution).

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one story part (start words, voices, something happens and a fix, an ending and making a new one); the adult paragraphs give the curriculum statements, the four-part story shape with its research basis, the named mistakes with a do-not-take-over caution, and what the lab does. No content-gate filler phrase matches; lab text is only instructions, character lines and feedback.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark for every step: the talk bubble, play mat and three start cards sit in separate bands with Teddy below; the three toy cards and three line cards fit in rows of three with two-line text; long problem and ending cards are full-width rows (fixed after a first pass where 3-across cards clipped 'Oh no! The wind blows…'); the 12-card mixer fits 4 rows of 3 with a 3-line story read-back box that no longer clips at the edges. Canvas is 1.36 times as tall as wide on phones; walk.cjs passed on iPhone 13 and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin: Pick <card> then Put it on <the talk bubble / play mat / toy / the tree / the end of the story>, tap-to-pick on the canvas too, and every mixer card and Tell my story is a labelled button. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each scene description and each piece of feedback, the challenge feedback is a role=status live region, right and wrong cards carry ✓ / ✗ text as well as colour, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found nothing in light or dark on desktop and phone.
